The House Committee on Regulated Industries offers the following substitute to SB 254/CSFA 254:
Senate Bill 254 By: Senator Cowsert of the 46th AS PASSED SENATE A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Chapter 23 of Title 2 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, the "Georgia Hemp Farming Act," so as to prohibit the sale of authorize licensed retail dealers in distilled spirits to obtain retail consumable hemp beverages that contain THC; establishment licenses; to provide milligram limits on THC authorize licensed retail dealers in distilled spirits to sell or offer for sale consumable hemp products; products to provide for a definition; consumers; to revise certain definitions; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1. Chapter 23 of Title 2 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, the "Georgia Hemp Farming Act," is amended in Code Section 2-23-3, relating to definitions, by adding a new paragraph to read as follows: "(28.1) 'Total THC' means delta-8-tetrahydrocannabinol, delta-9-THC, delta-10-tetrahydrocannabinol, or any combination thereof." SECTION 2. Said chapter is further amended by revising Code Section 2-23-9.2, relating to consumable hemp products, packaging, advertising, and distribution, as follows: SB 254/CSFA "2-23-9.2. (a) No consumable hemp product shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state unless such product is packaged in a container that: (1) Is not attractive to children; (2) Does not bear any reasonable resemblance to any existing candy, snack, or other food product that is widely distributed and familiar to the public; (3) Does not infringe on any trade dress, trademarks, branding, or other related materials as described in Code Section 10-1-450 or in Chapter 22 of Title 15 of the United States Code; and (4) Is tamper evident and child resistant. … the United States Code; or (4) Suggests that such product constitutes or contains low THC oil, as such term is defined in Code Section 16-12-190, or otherwise constitutes or contains medical marijuana or medical cannabis. (c)(1) As used in this subsection, subsection Code section, the term: (A) 'Food product' means any product intended to be consumed by humans for physical subsistence; provided, however, that such term shall not include gummies, consumable base oils, or products that constitute drinks or beverages. (B) 'Gummy' means a gelatinous substance in the form of a cube, sphere, prismatoid, ovoid, or other shape that is designed for human ingestion. SB 254/CSFA (2) No consumable hemp product shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state if such product constitutes or is a component of: (A) A food product; or (B) A drink or beverage that: (i) Contains that contains alcohol or constitutes an alcoholic beverage under Title 3; or (ii) Contains THC. 3. (3) Nothing in this subsection is intended to prohibit the sale or distribution of hemp that is contained within gummies or consumable base oils, provided that such gummies or consumable base oils are not a component of a food product or a drink or beverage. (d)(1) Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2) and (3) product. (d) Notwithstanding any provision of this subsection, no chapter, any provision of Title 3, or any rules and regulations promulgated by the Commissioner of the Department of Revenue pursuant to Chapter 4 of Title 3, a licensed retail dealer in distilled spirits may obtain a retail consumable hemp product shall be sold establishment license and, upon obtaining such license, such licensed retail dealer may sell or otherwise distributed in this state if such product has more than: (A) Ten milligrams of total THC per serving; or (B) 150 milligrams of total THC per container. (2) No offer for sale consumable hemp product that is intended for topical application shall be sold or otherwise distributed products to consumers in accordance with the provisions of this state if such product is packaged in a container that has more than 1,000 milligrams of total THC. (3) No consumable hemp product that constitutes a tincture shall be sold or otherwise distributed in chapter and the rules and regulations promulgated by the Commissioner pursuant to this state if such product: (A) Has more than one milligram of total THC per one milliliter of liquid, or the proportionate equivalent thereof; or (B) Is packaged in a container that exceeds 60 milliliters of liquid." chapter."
SECTION 3. 2. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
